tooltip_popover.title: Indian System of Numeration
tooltip_popover.description: Uses periods of Thousands, Lakhs (1,00,000 = 10^5), and Crores (1,00,00,000 = 10^7).
tooltip_popover.example: Patna's population is 25 Lakhs (25,00,000); Mumbai's population is 2 Crores (2,00,00,000).

tooltip_popover.title: International System of Numeration
tooltip_popover.description: Uses periods of Thousands, Millions (1,000,000 = 10^6), and Billions (1,000,000,000 = 10^9).
tooltip_popover.example: 1 Million = 10 Lakhs; 1 Crore = 10 Millions; 1 Billion = 100 Crores.

tooltip_popover.title: Multiplication by 5 via Halving
tooltip_popover.description: To multiply an even number N by 5, halve the number and multiply by 10: N * 5 = (N / 2) * 10.

tooltip_popover.title: Multiplication by 25 via Quartering
tooltip_popover.description: To multiply a multiple of 4 N by 25, divide by 4 and multiply by 100: N * 25 = (N / 4) * 100.

tooltip_popover.title: Sequential Natural Number Digit Counts
tooltip_popover.description: Single-digit numbers (1-9) consume 9 total positions.
tooltip_popover.example: Finding the 100th digit: 100 - 9 = 91 digits from 2-digit numbers. 91 / 2 = 45 with remainder 1. 9 + 45 = 54. Next number is 55, whose first digit is 5.

image_asset.title: Place Value Systems & Shortcut Factor Scaling Diagram
image_asset.description: Comparative chart of Indian vs International numeration systems with factor shortcuts for multiplying by 5 and 25.

hotspots.title: Indian Place Value System
hotspots.popover_content: Lakh = 10^5, Crore = 10^7. Commas placed after 3 digits from right, then every 2 digits.

hotspots.title: International Place Value System
hotspots.popover_content: Million = 10^6, Billion = 10^9. Commas placed every 3 digits. 1 Crore = 10 Millions.

hotspots.title: Factor Shortcuts (x5 and x25)
hotspots.popover_content: N * 5 = (N / 2) * 10. N * 25 = (N / 4) * 100. Halve and scale by 10, or quarter and scale by 100.

hotspots.title: Sequential Digit Position Analytics
hotspots.popover_content: Digits 1-9 take 9 positions; 10-99 take 180 positions. Finding position 100 yields digit 5.

tooltip_popover.title: Operational Terms and Order
tooltip_popover.description: An expression combines numbers and operational signs (+, -, *, /).
tooltip_popover.example: In 39 - 2 * 6 + 11, evaluate term 2 * 6 = 12 first, giving 39 - 12 + 11 = 38.

tooltip_popover.title: Bracket Grouping Constraints
tooltip_popover.description: Brackets group sub-expressions into single compound terms to explicitly mandate evaluation priority.
tooltip_popover.example: Queen Alia's coin gift: (100 * 2) + (100 / 2) = 200 + 50 = 250 gold coins.

tooltip_popover.title: Commutative and Associative Laws
tooltip_popover.description: Commutative Addition: a + b = b + a.

tooltip_popover.title: Distributive Law of Multiplication
tooltip_popover.description: Multiplication distributes over addition: a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c.
tooltip_popover.example: Melvin's story reading: 8 * (7 - 2) = 8*7 - 8*2 = 56 - 16 = 40 stories.

tooltip_popover.title: Subtraction as Adding Additive Inverses
tooltip_popover.description: Subtracting a number is equivalent to adding its negative counterpart: a - b = a + (-b).
tooltip_popover.example: 18 - 10 = 18 + (-10) = 8; Token model combining 18 blue (+1) and 10 red (-1) tokens leaves 8 blue tokens.

image_asset.title: Term Partitioning, Laws & Zero-Pair Token Model Diagram
image_asset.description: Visual diagram demonstrating term partitioning, algebraic laws, zero-pair token modeling, and bracket negation.

hotspots.title: Term Partitioning & Order
hotspots.popover_content: Addition and subtraction signs partition expressions into individual terms evaluated before summation.

hotspots.title: Algebraic Laws of Arithmetic
hotspots.popover_content: Commutative: a+b=b+a. Associative: (a+b)+c=a+(b+c). Distributive: a*(b+c)=ab+ac.

hotspots.title: Zero-Pair Token Model
hotspots.popover_content: Subtracting b is adding its additive inverse: a-b = a+(-b). 18 blue (+1) + 10 red (-1) = 8 blue.

hotspots.title: Bracket Negation Rules
hotspots.popover_content: Negating a bracket flips internal signs: -(a+b) = -a-b and -(a-b) = -a+b.

tooltip_popover.title: Tenths, Hundredths, and Thousandths
tooltip_popover.description: Tenth = 1/10 = 0.1; Hundredth = 1/100 = 0.01; Thousandth = 1/1000 = 0.001.
tooltip_popover.example: 3.47 = 3 ones + 4 tenths + 7 hundredths = 3 + 4/10 + 7/100.

tooltip_popover.title: Currency and Length Conversions
tooltip_popover.description: Currency: 1 Rupee = 100 Paise => 1 Paise = ₹0.01 (e.g., 45 p = ₹0.45).
tooltip_popover.example: Honeybee body length: Head 2.3 cm + Thorax 5.4 cm + Abdomen 7.5 cm = 15.2 cm total.

tooltip_popover.title: Equivalent Decimals and Vertical Alignment
tooltip_popover.description: Appending trailing zeros to decimal places preserves value (0.2 = 0.20 = 0.200).
tooltip_popover.example: Comparing 0.2 and 0.09: 0.2 has 2 tenths while 0.09 has 0 tenths, so 0.2 > 0.09.

hotspots.title: Millimeter Subdivisions
hotspots.popover_content: 1 cm = 10 mm => 1 mm = 0.1 cm. Sub-unit subdivisions allow measuring exact fractional lengths.

hotspots.title: Expanded Decimal Grid
hotspots.popover_content: Place values right of decimal: Tenths (0.1), Hundredths (0.01), Thousandths (0.001).

hotspots.title: Equivalent Decimals & Alignment
hotspots.popover_content: Trailing zeros do not alter value: 0.2 = 0.20 = 0.200. Always align decimal points vertically.

tooltip_popover.title: Letter-Numbers and Perimeter Formulas
tooltip_popover.description: A letter-number (variable) represents an unspecified, changing numerical value.
tooltip_popover.example: Shabnam's age s in terms of Aftab's age a: s = a + 3.

tooltip_popover.title: Combining Like Terms
tooltip_popover.description: Like terms contain identical variables (e.g., 5y and 2y) and combine via numerical coefficients: 5y + 2y = 7y.
tooltip_popover.example: Simplify: 5y + x + x + 5y - 6 + 2 = 10y + 2x - 4.

children.label: Matchstick Square and Endless Grid Rules

tooltip_popover.title: Matchstick Square and Endless Grid Rules
tooltip_popover.description: Matchstick squares rule: w connected squares require 3w + 1 matchsticks.
tooltip_popover.example: For 10 squares: 3(10) + 1 = 31 matchsticks.

hotspots.title: Polygon Perimeters
hotspots.popover_content: Equilateral Triangle = 3s, Square = 4s, Regular Pentagon = 5s, Regular Hexagon = 6s.

hotspots.title: Matchstick Square Rule
hotspots.popover_content: Building w connected squares requires 3w + 1 matchsticks (1st square takes 4, each added takes 3).

hotspots.title: Endless 4-Column Grid Formula
hotspots.popover_content: Number N in row r, col c: N = 4(r - 1) + c = 4r - 4 + c. 143 lies in Row 36, Column 3.

hotspots.title: Combining Like Terms
hotspots.popover_content: Like terms share identical variables: 5y + 2y = 7y. Unlike terms (3x + 4y) cannot be merged.

tooltip_popover.title: Vertically Opposite Angles and Linear Pairs
tooltip_popover.description: Two straight lines intersect at at most one unique point, forming four angles.
tooltip_popover.example: If intersecting angle a = 35°, adjacent angle b = 180° - 35° = 145°, vertically opposite angle c = 35°, angle d = 145°.

tooltip_popover.title: Equidistant Parallelism and Orthogonality
tooltip_popover.description: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never meet, maintaining constant perpendicular distance throughout.
tooltip_popover.example: Opposite edges of a ruler, railway tracks.

tooltip_popover.title: Paper Folding Constructions
tooltip_popover.description: Successive parallel horizontal paper folds produce parallel line creases.
tooltip_popover.example: Folding square paper in half repeatedly creates parallel grid line creases.

image_asset.title: Intersecting Lines, Parallel Lines & Crease Geometry Diagram

hotspots.title: Intersecting Lines & Angles
hotspots.popover_content: Vertically opposite angles are equal (∠a = ∠c). Linear pairs sum to 180° (∠a + ∠b = 180°).

hotspots.title: Parallel Lines (l || m)
hotspots.popover_content: Coplanar lines that never meet. Maintain constant perpendicular distance throughout.

hotspots.title: Perpendicular Lines (l ⊥ m)
hotspots.popover_content: Lines that intersect at right angles (90°), forming 4 orthogonal quadrants.

hotspots.title: Paper Folding Creases
hotspots.popover_content: Successive horizontal folds yield parallel line creases; orthogonal fold creates perpendicular crease.

tooltip_popover.title: Taller-in-Front Callout Rule
tooltip_popover.description: Children in line report the count of individuals standing ahead who are strictly taller.
tooltip_popover.example: Callout sequence (0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 0, 3) uniquely reconstructs 7 stick figures by height.

tooltip_popover.title: Even and Odd Operational Laws
tooltip_popover.description: Even = 2n; Odd = 2n - 1.
tooltip_popover.example: Sum of 50 odd numbers is always EVEN.

tooltip_popover.title: 3x3 Magic Square Constraints
tooltip_popover.description: An n x n grid filled with distinct integers where every row, column, and diagonal sums to the same constant.
tooltip_popover.example: Standard magic square row 1: [8, 1, 6], row 2: [3, 5, 7], row 3: [4, 9, 2].

hotspots.title: Height Line Logic
hotspots.popover_content: Callout number = count of taller individuals standing ahead. Tallest person calls out 0.

hotspots.title: Integer Parity Algebra
hotspots.popover_content: Even = 2n, Odd = 2n-1. Odd + Odd = Even. Loose leaf page sum = (2k-1)+2k = 4k-1 (Always ODD).

hotspots.title: 3x3 Magic Square Proof
hotspots.popover_content: Magic constant S = 15. Center cell x belongs to 4 lines: 45 + 3x = 60 => x = 5. Exactly 8 rotations.

hotspots.title: Cryptarithms & Elimination
hotspots.popover_content: Letter substitution puzzles solved using place-value digit constraints and parity elimination.

d3_react_flow_tree.label: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

tooltip_popover.title: Triangle Inequality Theorem
tooltip_popover.description: Three pairwise intersecting lines form a triangle.
tooltip_popover.example: Sides 5, 10, 12: 5 + 10 = 15 > 12 (Triangle Exists).

tooltip_popover.title: Equilateral, Isosceles, and Scalene Types
tooltip_popover.description: Equilateral: All 3 sides equal (a = b = c). Always constructible for any s > 0 because s + s = 2s > s.
tooltip_popover.example: Equilateral triangle with sides 50 cm, 50 cm, 50 cm; Scalene triangle with sides 24 cm, 26 cm, 28 cm.

image_asset.chapter_title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

image_asset.description: Direct path vs detour geometry, triangle inequality theorem, side classification, and compass arc feasibility.

hotspots.title: Direct Path vs Detour
hotspots.popover_content: Direct straight path c is strictly shorter than detour path a + b (c < a + b => a + b > c).

hotspots.title: Triangle Inequality Theorem
hotspots.popover_content: Sum of any 2 sides > 3rd side (a+b>c, b+c>a, c+a>b). Test: Smallest two sum > longest side.

hotspots.title: Side-Based Classification
hotspots.popover_content: Equilateral (a=b=c, always valid for s>0), Isosceles (a=b!=c), Scalene (a!=b!=c).

hotspots.title: Compass Arc Construction
hotspots.popover_content: Compass arcs of radii a and b intersect to locate 3rd vertex iff a + b > c. Arcs fail if a + b <= c.

tooltip_popover.title: Brahmagupta's Multiplication Formula (628 CE)
tooltip_popover.description: To multiply fractions, multiply numerators together and denominators together: (a / b) * (c / d) = (a * c) / (b * d).
tooltip_popover.example: (2/3) * (4/5) = 8/15; Area model with 3/4 x 2/3 overlapping grid = 6/12 = 1/2.

tooltip_popover.title: Division via Reciprocals
tooltip_popover.description: Dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: (a / b) / (c / d) = (a / b) * (d / c).
tooltip_popover.example: Maria decorating bags: 8 m / (1/4 m per bag) = 8 * 4 = 32 bags.

tooltip_popover.title: Telescoping Cancellation Pattern
tooltip_popover.description: In products of the form (1 - 1/2)(1 - 1/3)(1 - 1/4)...(1 - 1/n), adjacent numerators and denominators cancel out completely.

image_asset.title: Brahmagupta Area Model & Telescoping Series Diagram
image_asset.description: Brahmagupta's fraction multiplication rule, 1x1 area grid model, reciprocal division, and telescoping series cancellation.

hotspots.title: Brahmagupta's Rule (628 CE)
hotspots.popover_content: (a/b) * (c/d) = (a*c)/(b*d). Multiply numerators together and denominators together. Area model overlap.

hotspots.title: Reciprocal Division & Scaling
hotspots.popover_content: (a/b) / (c/d) = (a/b) * (d/c). Dividing by proper fraction (<1) ENLARGES the quotient value.

hotspots.title: Real-World Fraction Scaling
hotspots.popover_content: Lace bags: 8 m / (1/4 m) = 32 bags. Tank fill time: 1 / (7/10) = 10/7 hours = 1 3/7 hrs.
